blind.why: Top-down mesh plotted the same way (blue fill, yellow area borders) against CS2 Dust2 (awpy). The CS2 mesh is made of polygons that follow walls and props, with an even clearance border, and box tops are included. Ours is a 0.5 m staircase grid with ragged borders and notched pockets in wall corners. Box tops a player can mantle onto (up to 1.62 m) are missing because there are no mantle links (jump-up max 1.1 m).

Two routes, spawn to site, in the same plot format. Ours are clean any-angle string-pulled lines that read like a human route. The CS2 render only shows a jagged corridor of triangles, not a smoothed path.

Chosen cover vs a real CS2 cover moment. Ours (A site, threat on Long Ramp): the cover point really is behind the crate stack and its peek spot is 1 m to the side, so it is correct. But it is one big flat crate in an empty square. CS2 shows layered prop cover a player actually crouches behind.

biggest_gap: Tactical and path query cost tails will stall the main thread. On the real map (load avg ~28 on 4 cores) holdSpots(A site, toward Long Ramp, 12) took 176 ms and holdSpots(B, toward Tunnel Mouth) 350 ms per call. coverPoints took 5-21 ms. path() with noCache had p50 0.4 ms but p95 4.6-21 ms and max 46-264 ms over 3000 random pairs. Your own validator in the same session gave p95 5.7 ms / max 11.8 ms. One bot choosing a hold spot = a visible frame hitch. Fix: precompute per-node hold and cover candidates at build time (or time-slice them like requestPath), cap A* expansions, add a hierarchical/area-level search so long routes stay under ~0.5 ms. CS2 bots read precomputed nav-area hiding spots and encounter spots and never ray-scan per query.
other_gaps: Hop-over paths: 17 of 400 random paths (4%) jump onto an obstacle and drop off at the same level instead of walking around. Repro: path (3.75,0,-42.75)->(14.25,0,-22.75) goes over the 0.75 m planter at (10.75,0.75,-36) in East Room. Same at (-18.75,0.55,-35) and (6.75,0.75,-25.5). It looks bot-like and fails with a follower that only jumps on flag 1. Raise the cost of jump-then-drop over short obstacles.
No mantle links: the player can mantle 1.62 m but nav jump-up stops at 1.1 m. Box and ledge tops a human uses (boost and off-angle spots) are missing from the nav, so bots can never hold them.

Coverage gaps at wall corners and doorway pockets: in 8800 player-sim wander samples, 6.5% of standable spots have no nav node within 1 m (corner clusters at (-44,*,-44), (40,2,-44), (8,0,48), (32,0,0), (-16,0,-16)). These are exactly the tight corner spots players hold.
Build time is 0.83 s in the validator and 1.9-4.5 s in-page under load, all on the main thread, so a map change or a collider-signature change hitches. Time-slice or move it to a Worker.

Debug overlay is hard to read. view=top/iso keeps the HUD (minimap, crosshair, ammo, scoreboard) on top, the skyline is not hidden, the map fills about 40% of the frame, and area labels, jump links, cover cones and sample paths cannot be read at that scale. The in-world overlay (draw(true)) is a wall of magenta jump fans.

Rare traversal failures with a naive pure-pursuit follower: 5 of 3000 (0.17%). Cases: Long Doors start (36.25,0,21.25) blocked by the produce stall within 0.4 m; after the Hub Ledge drop at (-7.75,0,-12.75) the next 12 m straight segment grazes the pillar at (-4.4,0,-14); (-44.25,1.2,-40.25) Balcony approach; (-2.7,0.6,-36.3) step.
bugs: tools/nav_validate.mjs --map=game exits RESULT: FAIL: 10 paths clip a headroom seam at (26,1.5,-32), pair ids 80, 435, 493, 590, 871, 1290, 1327, 1407, 1606, 1726. The nav still routes through it instead of excluding it.
holdSpots returns exposure values of 0.79-4.42 although the API documents exposure as a 0..1 fraction.
holdSpots(A site, toward Ember spawn) returns [] (no fallback when the threat point is out of sight).
strengths: Walked with the game's own simulate() and capsule collision: 2995/3000 random pairs arrived, at 0.139 s/m (about 7.2 m/s, full run speed), so nothing slows from scraping walls.
Fully deterministic: node hash and path hash identical across two page loads.
Smoothed paths are clean any-angle lines; median detour 1.19x over straight-line distance (p95 2.04x).
Eye-to-eye visibility costs about 23 us per query and respects Haze smoke (true before the smoke, false after).
Cover points are genuinely hidden from the threat (expo 0) and their peek spots are genuinely visible. Area callouts flood correctly (39 areas). No console errors.
